questions.question: Where was the first jute mill set up at Kolkata in 1859?
questions.solution:
The first jute mill was established at Rishra (near Kolkata) in 1859 by George Acland.
  • Jute is known as the 'Golden Fibre'.
  • India is the world's largest producer of raw jute.

questions.question: Moved by the Swadeshi Movement, ______ painted his famous image of Bharat Mata portraying her as an ascetic figure.
questions.solution:
Abanindranath Tagore painted the iconic Bharat Mata in 1905 during the Swadeshi Movement.
  • The image depicts her as a four-armed deity in saffron robes, holding a book, sheaves of paddy, a white cloth, and a mala.
  • He was the founder of the 'Indian Society of Oriental Art'.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts was enacted in British India in the year 1878?
questions.option_3: East India Stock Dividend Redemption Act
questions.solution:
The Vernacular Press Act was passed by Lord Lytton in 1878 to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press.
  • It was also known as the Gagging Act.
  • The Arms Act of 1878 was also enacted in the same year.

questions.question: Which of the following books was written by James Mill, a Scottish economist, in 1817?
questions.option_2: The History of British in India
questions.option_3: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
questions.solution:
Scottish economist James Mill published 'A History of British India' in 1817.
  • He famously divided Indian history into three periods: Hindu, Muslim, and British.
  • He was a proponent of Utilitarianism.

questions.question: Which of the following princely states was annexed by the British under the pretext of 'misgovernment of the Nawab'?
questions.solution:
Awadh was annexed in 1856 by Lord Dalhousie under the pretext of 'maladministration'.
  • The ruler at that time was Wajid Ali Shah.
  • Other states like Satara and Jhansi were annexed via the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.question: Who was made the Nawab of Bengal following the Battle of Plassey?
questions.solution:
Mir Jafar was placed on the throne of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey (1757).
  • He betrayed Siraj-ud-daulah to help the British.
  • He is often referred to as a traitor in Indian history.

questions.question: In which year was the partition of Bengal carried out by the British Viceroy Lord Curzon?
questions.solution:
The Partition of Bengal was carried out in 1905 by Lord Curzon.
  • The official reason was administrative convenience, but the real aim was to weaken the nationalist movement.
  • It was annulled in 1911.

questions.question: Who emerged victorious in ‘The Siege of Arcot’ in 1751 AD?
questions.solution:
The British (led by Robert Clive) emerged victorious in the Siege of Arcot (1751).
  • This was a turning point in the Second Carnatic War.
  • It established British supremacy over the French in South India.

questions.question: In which year was the National Archives of India established?
questions.solution:
The National Archives of India (NAI) was established in 1891 at Calcutta as the Imperial Record Department.
  • It was moved to New Delhi in 1911.
  • It is the custodian of the non-current records of the Government of India.

questions.question: Who among the following revolutionaries was popularly known as 'Master Da'?
questions.solution:
Surya Sen was a revolutionary leader popularly known as 'Master Da'.
  • He led the Chittagong Armoury Raid in 1930.
  • He was a school teacher by profession.

questions.question: In the context of Sufi traditions, the term 'sama' stood for:
questions.solution:
In Sufi traditions, Sama refers to the recital of holy songs to induce a state of spiritual ecstasy.
  • It often involves music and dance (whirling).
  • The place where Sufis gathered was called a Khanqah.

questions.question: In the context of Gupta administration, the term 'vithi' referred to a/an:
questions.solution:
During the Gupta period, Vithi was an administrative unit equivalent to a sub-district.
  • The hierarchy was: Desha (Province) > Bhukti > Vishaya (District) > Vithi > Grama (Village).

questions.question: Rulers of mahajanapadas in ancient India collected a tax called ‘Bhaga’ from the ______ in their region.
questions.solution:
The 'Bhaga' tax was collected from farmers and usually amounted to 1/6th of the produce.
  • It was the main source of income for the Mahajanapada rulers.
  • Other taxes included Bali (voluntary/mandatory offerings).

questions.question: ‘Microliths’ were ______ used by early humans.
questions.solution:
Microliths are small stone tools, typically 1 to 5 cm long, used during the Mesolithic Age.
  • They were often fixed to handles of bone or wood to make saws and sickles.

questions.question: The river Indus was called ______ by the Iranians and the Greeks about 2500 years ago.
questions.solution:
The Iranians and Greeks called the Indus River 'Hindos' or 'Indos' about 2,500 years ago.
  • The land to the east of the river was called India.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Palaeolithic site of archaeological importance in India?
questions.solution:
Hunasagi is a significant Palaeolithic site located in Karnataka.
  • Archaeologists found a large number of tools made from limestone here.
  • Mehrgarh and Burzahom are Neolithic sites.

questions.question: Ancient Indian manuscripts were usually written on palm leaves or the bark of the ______ tree, which grows in the Himalayas.
questions.solution:
Ancient manuscripts were written on palm leaves or the bark of the Birch tree (Bhurjapatra).
  • These trees grow predominantly in the Himalayas.

questions.question: ‘Harshacharita’ (The Deeds of Harsha), which is the biography of Indian Emperor Harsha, was written by _______.
questions.solution:
The 'Harshacharita' is the biography of Emperor Harshavardhana written by his court poet Banabhatta.
  • Banabhatta also wrote 'Kadambari'.
  • Harsha belonged to the Pushyabhuti dynasty.

questions.question: Which place had water harvesting system channeling the flood water of the Ganga river in the first century B.C?
questions.solution:
Sringaverapura (near Prayagraj) had a sophisticated water harvesting system in the 1st century B.C.
  • It utilized a series of tanks to channel and filter the floodwaters of the Ganga.

questions.question: Under the rule of which king was the Sun Temple at Konark built?
questions.solution:
The Sun Temple at Konark was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty in the 13th century.
  • It is also known as the 'Black Pagoda'.
  • It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: The two epics, ‘Raghuvamsha’ and ‘Kumarasambhava’ are works of ______.
questions.solution:
Kalidasa, the 'Shakespeare of India', wrote Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava.
  • He was one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) in the court of Chandragupta II.
  • His other famous works include Abhigyanashakuntalam and Meghaduta.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first English language newspaper of India?
questions.solution:
Hicky's Bengal Gazette, started in 1780 by James Augustus Hicky, was India's first newspaper.
  • It was an English-language weekly published in Calcutta.

questions.question: In which of the following cities was the Veda Samaj established in 1864?
questions.solution:
The Veda Samaj was established in Madras (Chennai) in 1864.
  • It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and led by Chembeti Sridharalu Naidu.
  • It worked against caste distinctions and promoted widow remarriage.

questions.question: When did the Indian Army liberate Goa from the Portuguese and declare it a Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The Indian Army liberated Goa from Portuguese rule in 1961 through Operation Vijay.
  • Goa was a Union Territory until it became a state in 1987.
  • The Portuguese were the first Europeans to arrive and the last to leave India.

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Salbai signed?
questions.solution:
The Treaty of Salbai was signed in 1782, ending the First Anglo-Maratha War.
  • It established a period of peace between the British and Marathas for 20 years.
